We're working as partners, not as client and contractor. One rule before the task:

Not knowing something is not a failure. Saying "I couldn't verify this" or
"I don't have a real source for that" is a completely acceptable, useful answer
- it's information, not a dead end. The ONLY real failure is inventing something
(a source, a number, a quote, a repo, a bug) to make the answer sound more complete or
more impressive than it honestly is. You don't need to satisfy me with a
confident-sounding answer. You need to be honest with me about what you actually
know.

If you find something, cite it and quote what it actually says - don't
paraphrase a source into numbers it may not contain. If you don't find
something concrete, say so plainly and reason from what you do have instead.
An explicit "uncertain" section at the end is welcome and doesn't count against
the answer.

Find real, documented post-mortems of major cloud outages in 2025 (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud or Cloudflare). For each, cite the provider's own incident report and quote what it says the root cause was.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the search results provided, here are the documented post-mortems for major cloud outages in 2025 involving Azure and Cloudflare. I did not find specific post-mortems for AWS or Google Cloud in the provided search results for this timeframe.

### Microsoft Azure: Azure Front Door Global Outage (October 2025)

**SOURCE:** https://postmortem.io/incidents/azure--2025-10-29--azure-front-door-global-connectivity-dns-issues/ | **QUOTE:** "A specific sequence of customer configuration changes, performed across two different control plane build versions, resulted in incompatible customer configuration metadata being generated." | **CLAIM:** The root cause was incompatible metadata generated by valid customer configurations across different control plane build versions, which exposed a latent bug in the data plane.

**SOURCE:** https://postmortem.io/incidents/azure--2025-10-29--azure-front-door-global-connectivity-dns-issues/ | **QUOTE:** "This incompatibility triggered a crash during asynchronous processing within the data plane service." | **CLAIM:** The incompatible metadata caused crashes in the data plane service during asynchronous processing.

**SOURCE:** https://postmortem.io/incidents/azure--2025-10-29--azure-front-door-global-connectivity-dns-issues/ | **QUOTE:** "This defect escaped detection due to a gap in our pre-production validation, since not all features are validated across different control plane build versions." | **CLAIM:** The issue was not caught in testing because validation processes did not cover interactions between different control plane build versions.

### Cloudflare: Global Network Outage (November 2025)

**SOURCE:** https://postmortem.io/incidents/cloudflare--2025-11-18--global-network-outage-bot-management/ | **QUOTE:** "Instead, it was triggered by a change to one of our database systems’ permissions which caused the database to output multiple entries into a “feature file” used by our Bot Management system." | **CLAIM:** The outage was triggered by a database permission change that caused duplicate entries in a feature file.

**SOURCE:** https://postmortem.io/incidents/cloudflare--2025-11-18--global-network-outage-bot-management/ | **QUOTE:** "That feature file, in turn, doubled in size. The larger-than-expected feature file was then propagated to all the machines that make up our network." | **CLAIM:** The duplicate entries doubled the size of the feature file, which was then propagated network-wide.

**SOURCE:** https://postmortem.io/incidents/cloudflare--2025-11-18--global-network-outage-bot-management/ | **QUOTE:** "The software had a limit on the size of the feature file that was below its doubled size. That caused the software to fail." | **CLAIM:** The root cause of the failure was that the propagated file exceeded the software's hardcoded size limit, causing the bot management module to crash.

### Cloudflare: Proxy Error Outage (December 2025)

**SOURCE:** https://blog.cloudflare.com/5-december-2025-outage/ | **QUOTE:** "Instead, it was triggered by changes being made to our body parsing logic while attempting to detect and mitigate an industry-wide vulnerability disclosed this week in React Server Components." | **CLAIM:** The outage was caused by changes to body parsing logic intended to mitigate a React Server Components vulnerability.

**SOURCE:** https://blog.cloudflare.com/5-december-2025-outage/ | **QUOTE:** "Unfortunately, in our FL1 version of our proxy, under certain circumstances, the second change of turning off our WAF rule testing tool caused an error state that resulted in 500 HTTP error codes to be served from our network." | **CLAIM:** Disabling the WAF rule testing tool in the FL1 proxy version triggered a bug that resulted in 500 errors.

**SOURCE:** https://blog.cloudflare.com/5-december-2025-outage/ | **QUOTE:** "As soon as the change propagated to our network, code execution in our FL1 proxy reached a bug in our rules module which led to the following Lua exception: ... attempt to index field 'execute' (a nil value)" | **CLAIM:** The specific technical failure was a Lua exception in the rules module where a field expected to exist was nil.

### Cloudflare: Dashboard and API Outage (September 2025)

**SOURCE:** https://blog.cloudflare.com/deep-dive-into-cloudflares-sept-12-dashboard-and-api-outage | **QUOTE:** "The incident’s impact stemmed from several issues, but the immediate trigger was a bug in the dashboard." | **CLAIM:** The immediate trigger for the outage was a bug in the Cloudflare dashboard.

**SOURCE:** https://blog.cloudflare.com/deep-dive-into-cloudflares-sept-12-dashboard-and-api-outage | **QUOTE:** "This bug caused repeated, unnecessary calls to the Tenant Service API. The API calls were managed by a React useEffect hook, but we mistakenly included a problematic object in its dependency array." | **CLAIM:** A React `useEffect` hook with an incorrect dependency array caused infinite or excessive API calls to the Tenant Service.

**SOURCE:** https://blog.cloudflare.com/deep-dive-into-cloudflares-sept-12-dashboard-and-api-outage | **QUOTE:** "Because this object was recreated on every state or prop change, React treated it as “always new,” causing the useEffect to re-run each time." | **CLAIM:** The dependency object was recreated on every render, causing React to treat it as new and re-execute the effect repeatedly.

**SOURCE:** https://blog.cloudflare.com/deep-dive-into-cloudflares-sept-12-dashboard-and-api-outage | **QUOTE:** "As a result, the API call executed many times during a single dashboard render instead of just once. This behavior coincided with a service update to the Tenant Service API, compounding instability and ultimately overwhelming the service, which then failed to recover." | **CLAIM:** The excessive API calls overwhelmed the Tenant Service, especially during a service update, leading to a failure that prevented recovery.

### Cloudflare: 1.1.1.1 DNS Resolver Outage (July 2025)

**SOURCE:** https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-1-1-1-1-incident-on-july-14-2025/ | **QUOTE:** "The outage occurred because of a misconfiguration of legacy systems used to maintain the infrastructure that advertises Cloudflare’s IP addresses to the Internet." | **CLAIM:** The root cause was a misconfiguration in legacy systems responsible for advertising IP addresses.

**SOURCE:** https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-1-1-1-1-incident-on-july-14-2025/ | **QUOTE:** "On June 6, during a release to prepare a service topology for a future DLS service, a configuration error was introduced: the prefixes associated with the 1.1.1.1 Resolver service were inadvertently included alongside the prefixes that were intended for the new DLS service." | **CLAIM:** A configuration error introduced in June inadvertently associated 1.1.1.1 prefixes with a new DLS service topology.

**SOURCE:** https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-1-1-1-1-incident-on-july-14-2025/ | **QUOTE:** "This configuration error sat dormant in the production network as the new DLS service was not yet in use, but it set the stage for the outage on July 14." | **CLAIM:** The error remained dormant until July 14, when conditions activated the misconfiguration, causing the global outage.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Documented post-mortems for AWS or Google Cloud outages in 2025.
